mainTopic: How far a spreading fire creates liability, and whether one pays for hidden items burned in a grain stack.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the previous discussion, which say that pools of water in the ground do not split a field. Then a new משנה asks how far a fire lit on one's own land can spread and still make him liable. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא each give a fixed distance. רבי שמעון says everything depends on the fire. The גמרא challenges him from a משנה about oven distances, where he does seem to use fixed measurements. רבה בר אבוה answers that the limit depends on the size of the fire, and שמואל rules like רבי שמעון. A second משנה deals with vessels hidden in a burning grain stack: רבי יהודה makes him pay for them and the חכמים do not, though they agree about a burned house. רב כהנא and רבא explain where the two sides argue, and a ברייתא adds that the vessels' space is valued as if it were full of grain.

steps.title: Pools of water do not divide the field
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends: these waters are just 'pools of the land' and do not count as a separation in the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are just called pools of the land.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the very last line of the discussion from the previous page. It gives the final answer: these waters are only 'pools of the land.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they are only ordinary pools in the ground, they are not important enough to count as a real separation. The field is still treated as one field. After this line, a new משנה begins.

phrases.english: are called pools of the land.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the previous discussion. Being 'just pools' means they don't split the field into separate fields.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Pools of water in the ground are not a significant separation, so the field still counts as one field.

steps.title: How far can a fire travel and still create liability?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks: if someone lights a fire on his own land, up to what distance is he responsible when it spreads?
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone lights a fire inside his own property. How far may the fire travel for him still to be responsible?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a question. This sets up the next steps, where different תנאים give their answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lighting a fire on your own land is allowed. The question is how far it can spread before the damage is too far away to blame him. The answer has to be some limit, or perhaps no fixed limit at all.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lights or kindles a fire

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who kindles a fire within his own property,
up to how far may the fire travel?
phrases.notes: Meaning: how far can it spread and still make him responsible for the damage it does.

steps.triggerLanguage: המדליק בתוך שלו עד כמה תעבור הדליקה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum distance a fire may spread for the person who lit it to still be liable.

steps.title: Three opinions giving a fixed distance
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: picture him in the middle of a בית כור. רבי אליעזר: sixteen אמות, like a public road. רבי עקיבא: fifty אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: we view the fire as if it were in the middle of a בית כור. רבי אליעזר says: sixteen אמות, like the width of a public road. רבי עקיבא says: fifty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: Three תנאים answer the question, and each gives a set measurement for how far the fire's damage still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three agree there is a fixed limit. They only disagree about how big it is. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses half a בית כור, which is a large area. רבי אליעזר uses sixteen אמות, the width of a public road. רבי עקיבא says fifty אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: We view him / we picture it
An area of land large enough to plant a כּוֹר of seed

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaria says:
We view it as if it were
in the middle of a beit kor.
phrases.notes: If the fire stands in the center, he is responsible up to the edge of that area, which is half a בית כור in each direction.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: sixteen cubits,
like the width of a public road.
Rabbi Akiva says: fifty cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה אומר רואין אותו כאילו הוא באמצע בית כור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives answers to the משנה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three fixed limits: half a בית כור, sixteen אמות, or fifty אמות.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: it all depends on the fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from the פסוק 'שלם ישלם המבער את הבערה' that there is no fixed distance. Everything depends on the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'The one who lit the fire shall surely pay.' Everything depends on the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the other three and refuses to set one number. Each case depends on how big the fire is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a single measurement, רבי שמעון uses the פסוק to show that the person who lit the fire pays for whatever his fire could reach. A big fire travels farther, so the liability goes farther. This sounds as if רבי שמעון has no fixed measurements for fire at all, and the גמרא will question exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who lit or caused the fire

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives four views. Three set a fixed distance (half a בית כור, 16 אמות, 50 אמות). רבי שמעון says it all depends on the size of the fire.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"The one who kindled the fire shall surely pay"
everything is according to the fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי שמעון אומר שלם ישלם המבער את הבערה הכל לפי הדליקה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the three fixed-distance opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no fixed distance; liability depends on the size of the fire.

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון really have no fire measurement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does רבי שמעון really hold that there is no set measurement for fire?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Does רבי שמעון really not have a set measurement for fire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a surprised question about רבי שמעון's view. This sets up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the משנה it sounds as if רבי שמעון never uses fixed measurements for fire. The גמרא is about to point to a source suggesting that he does. The question sounds like a simple question, but it is really the start of an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: And does Rabbi Shimon not hold
of a fixed measure for fire?

steps.triggerLanguage: ולית ליה לרבי שמעון שיעורא בדליקה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי שמעון's view from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's statement that everything depends on the fire, with no fixed measure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other sources seem to show that רבי שמעון does accept fixed measurements for fire.

steps.title: The source: fixed distances for an oven and stove
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: an oven needs four אמות of space above it, an oven in an upper room needs three טפחים of plaster under it, a stove needs one טפח, and if it still causes damage he pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: A person may not set up an oven inside a house unless there are four אמות of height above it. If he sets it up in an upper room, there must be a layer of plaster three טפחים thick under it. For a stove, one טפח. And if it causes damage, he pays for what it damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that gives fixed safety measurements for fire. This is the source it will use to challenge רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה sets exact distances and thicknesses to keep an oven or stove from setting the house on fire. Those are fixed measurements for fire. The גמרא will next connect this source to רבי שמעון, which is where the real conflict will show.

keyTerms.meaning: A layer of plaster or packed material on a floor
A stove, smaller than an oven

steps.confusionAlert: The part of the משנה quoted so far does not mention רבי שמעון by name. His words come at the end of the quote, in the next step.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: A person may not set up
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא בתרא 20b.

phrases.english: an oven inside the house,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יֵשׁ עַל גַּבּוֹ
phrases.english: unless there is above it
a height of four cubits.
If he was setting it up in an upper room —
not until there is plaster beneath it
three handbreadths thick.
And for a stove — one handbreadth.
And if it caused damage — he pays for what it damaged.

steps.triggerLanguage: והתנן לא יעמיד אדם תנור בתוך הבית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the challenge raised in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That there are fixed measurements regarding fire, which seems to conflict with רבי שמעון's 'everything depends on the fire.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in בבא בתרא 20b about the required distances for an oven and stove.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says the oven distances exempt you
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה ends with רבי שמעון saying the oven and stove measurements teach that if you kept them and damage still happened, you are exempt. So he does seem to hold of fixed measurements.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: these measurements were only given to teach that if it caused damage, he is exempt from paying!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from step 6. The last line is the real point of the proof: רבי שמעון himself uses fixed distances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 רבי שמעון said fire has no fixed distance. But here he says that someone who kept the oven distances is exempt if damage happens anyway. That sounds like a fixed safety measure, which seems to contradict his first statement.
steps.confusionAlert: In the oven משנה, the חכמים (step 6) say you pay even if you kept the distances. רבי שמעון disagrees and says you are exempt. That disagreement is exactly why his words here look like he holds of fixed measurements.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
These measurements were not stated
phrases.notes: These are the oven and stove distances from step 6: four אמות, three טפחים, and one טפח.

phrases.english: except to teach that if it caused damage, he is exempt from paying!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: לֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ שִׁיעוּרִין הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quotation begun in step 6 and gives the line that actually makes the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון does hold of set measurements for fire
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about ovens and stoves, where רבי שמעון exempts someone who kept the required distances

steps.title: It all depends on the size of the fire
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, explains that רבי שמעון never said there are no measurements at all. He meant there is no single fixed distance, because the distance depends on how big the fire is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: everything depends on the height of the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. רבי שמעון's 'no fixed measure' means the measure changes with the size of the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, 'no fixed distance' does not mean 'no limit at all'. A small fire has a short limit and a big fire has a long one. The oven distances fit an ordinary oven fire, so the two statements of רבי שמעון agree.

keyTerms.meaning: height (here, how big the fire is)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the working rule for fire damage according to רבי שמעון: liability is measured by the size of the fire, not by one number for every case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
Everything depends on the height of the fire.
phrases.notes: He is explaining what רבי שמעון meant back in step 4.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 5–7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains what רבי שמעון meant: 'no measure' means no single fixed measure, not no limit at all.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי שמעון holds that fire has no limit at all, which clashes with the oven distances.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון holds the limit depends on the size of the fire. The oven distances fit an ordinary oven fire.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Two chains of teachers report in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like רבי שמעון. And so רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: we follow רבי שמעון, so fire liability depends on the size of the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same ruling comes from שמואל through two separate chains, one through רב יוסף and רב יהודה, and one through רב נחמן. Having two chains makes the ruling firm.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the distance at which you stop being liable for a spreading fire depends on how big the fire is. That is רבי שמעון's view, and the הלכה follows it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said in the name of Rav Yehuda, in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha is like Rabbi Shimon.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And likewise Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha is like Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the contradiction is solved, the גמרא gives the final ruling on the מחלוקת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: liability for a spreading fire depends on the size of the fire.

steps.title: New משנה: vessels hidden inside a burning grain stack
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: someone set fire to a stack of grain that had vessels inside, and they burned too. רבי יהודה says he pays for what was inside. The חכמים say he pays only for the stack of wheat or barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone sets fire to a stack of grain, and there were vessels in it and they burned, רבי יהודה says he pays for what was inside it. The חכמים say he pays only for a stack of wheat or of barley.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new question. When a fire burns hidden things, does the person who lit it pay for them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees he pays for the grain stack itself. They disagree only about the vessels hidden inside. רבי יהודה makes him pay for them too. The חכמים limit payment to the stack, as if it held only wheat or barley.
steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים do not say he is exempt altogether. He still pays for the grain stack. They only exempt him from paying for the hidden vessels.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who sets fire to a stack of grain,
and there were vessels in it, and they burned,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְשַׁלֵּם מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: he pays for what was inside it,
and the Sages say: he does not pay

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא גָּדִישׁ שֶׁל חִטִּין אוֹ שֶׁל שְׂעוֹרִין.
phrases.english: except for a stack of wheat or of barley.
phrases.notes: He pays for the stack only as grain, whichever kind it was, and not for the hidden vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּדְלִיק אֶת הַגָּדִישׁ, וְהָיוּ בּוֹ כֵּלִים וְדָלְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic: hidden items burned in a fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: he pays for the hidden vessels too. The חכמים: he pays only for the grain stack.

steps.title: A goat and a slave burned with the stack
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if a goat was tied to the stack and a slave stood near it, he is liable. If the slave was tied and the goat stood near, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a goat was tied to the stack and a slave was standing near it, and they burned with it, he must pay. If a slave was tied to it and a goat was near it, and they burned with it, he does not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from step 10 keeps going. It adds two cases where living things burned along with the stack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the goat is tied, it could not escape, so he pays for it. The slave was free to run away, so he is not treated as a killer. When the slave is tied, burning him counts as killing a person, and someone who deserves death does not also pay money, so he is exempt even for the goat.

keyTerms.meaning: Near, standing next to it (not tied)
Must pay / does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the tied slave makes him less guilty. He is exempt from paying money because he committed the much bigger crime of killing a person.

phrases.english: If a goat was tied to it,
phrases.notes: "It" is the stack of grain from the case in step 10.

phrases.english: and a slave was near it
and it burned along with it, he is liable.
If a slave was tied to it,
and a goat was near it
and it burned along with it, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה about burning a stack with things inside it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tied goat with a free slave nearby: liable. Tied slave with a free goat nearby: exempt.

steps.title: The חכמים agree when a building is burned
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree with רבי יהודה that someone who burns a building pays for everything inside it, because people normally keep things in houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים agree with רבי יהודה that if someone sets fire to a building, he pays for everything inside it, because people normally keep their things in houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by showing where the חכמים agree that he pays for things inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the חכמים said he pays only for the grain stack, not for the vessels hidden in it. A house is different, because it is normal to keep belongings there. So whoever burns a house should expect that things are inside.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree (here, they admit a point to the other side)

phrases.english: And the Sages agree with Rabbi Yehuda
about one who sets fire to a building,
that he pays for everything inside it;
since it is the normal way of people
to keep things in houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּמַדְלִיק אֶת הַבִּירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a case where the חכמים from step 10 agree with רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who burns a building pays for everything in it, according to everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים exempt hidden vessels in a field stack, but they agree he pays for everything inside a burned house.

steps.title: רב כהנא limits where the argument applies
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says the מחלוקת is only when the fire was lit on his own property and spread. If he lit it on his friend's property, everyone agrees he pays for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The argument is when someone lit a fire on his own land and it spread and burned on his friend's land. רבי יהודה makes him pay for hidden things the fire damaged, and the חכמים exempt him. But if he lit the fire on his friend's land, everyone agrees he pays for everything inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב כהנא explains which case the רבי יהודה and חכמים argument is really about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא narrows the מחלוקת. It is only about fire that spread, where the question is whether you pay for hidden things the fire reached. If you start the fire right in your friend's property, you are like someone damaging with his own hands, and everyone agrees you pay for all of it.

phrases.english: Gemara: Rav Kahana said:
The argument is about one who lights a fire on his own property
and it spread and burned things on his friend's property,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְחַיַּיב אַנִּזְקֵי טָמוּן בָּאֵשׁ,
phrases.english: since Rabbi Yehuda holds him liable for fire damage to hidden things,
and the Rabbis exempt him;
but one who lights the fire on his friend's property,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מְשַׁלֵּם כׇּל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ.
phrases.english: everyone agrees he pays for everything inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: מַחֲלוֹקֶת בְּמַדְלִיק בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first גמרא statement on the משנה; it defines the case of the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is only about fire that spread from one's own property. If he lit the fire on his friend's property, he pays for everything.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move, where רבא asks whether the wording of the משנה fits this reading.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה should have split the stack case itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if רב כהנא is right, why did the משנה switch to a building case? It should have taught the split inside the stack case itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, instead of teaching at the end, "The חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about burning a building, that he pays for everything inside, since people keep things in houses," the משנה should have made the split in the same case: "When is this said? When he lit the fire on his own land and it spread and burned on his friend's land. But if he lit it on his friend's land, everyone agrees he pays for everything that was inside!"
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב כהנא from the way the משנה is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים really agreed whenever the fire was lit on a friend's property, the easiest way to say so was inside the stack case. The משנה instead brings a different case, a building. That suggests the חכמים agree only in the case of a building, not just because of where the fire was lit.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what you said is true)
The last part of the משנה
Let it make a distinction and teach it
When is this said? (a phrase that limits a rule)

phrases.english: Rava said to him: If so,
instead of teaching the last part:
the Sages agree with Rabbi Yehuda
about one who sets fire to a building,
that he pays for everything inside it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן דֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם לְהַנִּיחַ בַּבָּתִּים;
phrases.english: since people normally keep things in houses;
let it make the distinction and teach it in the same case:
phrases.notes: "The same case" means the burning stack itself, without switching to a building.

phrases.english: When is this said?
When he lit the fire on his own property,
and it spread and burned on his friend's property;
but one who lights the fire on his friend's property,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מְשַׁלֵּם כׇּל מַה שֶּׁהָיָה בְּתוֹכוֹ!
phrases.english: everyone agrees he pays for everything that was inside it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִי הָכִי, אַדְּתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב כהנא's reading in step 13 using the wording of the משנה in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that everyone agrees he pays for everything when the fire was lit on a friend's property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the rule, the משנה would have taught it as a split inside the stack case. Bringing a separate building case shows the חכמים agree only about a building.

steps.title: רבא's new approach, first case: fire that spread from the burner's own property
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets aside רב כהנא's approach and says the two sides argue in two cases. The first case is a fire lit on one's own property that spread. Here רבי יהודה makes him pay for hidden items, and the רבנן exempt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: They argue about two things. They argue about someone who lights a fire on his own property, and it spreads and burns things on his friend's property. רבי יהודה makes him pay for things hidden in the fire, and the רבנן hold he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops רב כהנא's explanation and starts his own. He says there are two separate arguments, and this step gives the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא had said they argue only about a fire that spread, and agree when it was lit on the friend's property. רבא agrees about the spreading fire, but holds that the רבנן never fully agree in the stack case, even when the fire was lit on the friend's land (next step). That answers his question from step 14: the משנה could only teach full agreement with a building, not a stack.

keyTerms.meaning: Items hidden inside what burned, which could not be seen.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is agreeing with רב כהנא. The word אלא ('rather') shows he is replacing רב כהנא's view. In רבא's view they also argue when the fire was lit on the friend's property.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
They disagree about two things;
they disagree about one who lights a fire on his own property
and it spread and burned on his friend's property:
Rabbi Yehuda makes him liable for things hidden in the fire,
and the Rabbis hold he is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבא's own challenge in step 14 by replacing רב כהנא's explanation with a two-part one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier explanation with a new reading of the מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רב כהנא, there is no argument when the fire is lit on the friend's property, so the משנה should have taught that split inside the stack case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue in both settings. This first one is a spreading fire, where the question is whether he pays for hidden items at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fire lit on one's own property that spread: רבי יהודה makes him pay for hidden items, and the רבנן exempt him.

steps.title: רבא's second case: fire lit directly on the friend's property
steps.stepSummary: In the second case the fire was lit on the friend's property. Both sides agree he pays for some hidden items. רבי יהודה says he pays for everything, even a purse. The רבנן say he pays only for tools people normally keep in a stack.
steps.simpleTranslation: They also argue about someone who lights a fire on his friend's property. רבי יהודה holds he pays for everything inside, even a purse. The רבנן hold that he pays for vessels people normally hide in a stack, like threshing sledges and cattle yokes. For vessels people don't normally hide in a stack, he does not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the second argument, about a fire lit directly on the friend's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is no longer whether he pays for hidden items, since lighting it on the friend's land makes him liable for them. The question is which hidden items count. רבי יהודה says anything, even money. The רבנן say only farm tools a person would normally expect to find in a stack.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing sledges, farm tools for threshing grain.

steps.whatToRemember: In רבא's view there are two arguments. (1) A fire that spread from his own property: does he pay for hidden items at all? רבי יהודה says yes and the רבנן say no. (2) A fire lit on the friend's property: he pays for hidden items, but which ones? רבי יהודה says everything, even a purse. The רבנן say only things normally kept in a stack.

phrases.english: And they also disagree about one who lights a fire on his friend's property:
Rabbi Yehuda holds:

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁלֵּם כׇּל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ, וַאֲפִילּוּ אַרְנְקִי,
phrases.english: he pays for everything inside it, even a purse,
and the Rabbis hold:
vessels that are normally hidden in a stack,
such as threshing sledges and cattle yokes,
those are what he pays for;
vessels that are not normally hidden in a stack,
he does not pay for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's two-part explanation that began in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fire lit on the friend's property: רבי יהודה says he pays for all hidden items, even money. The רבנן say only for items normally stored in a stack.

steps.title: A ברייתא repeats the argument over vessels burned in a stack
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings the same מחלוקת as the משנה. רבי יהודה says he pays for everything inside the stack. The חכמים say he pays only for a stack of wheat or barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone lights a stack, and there were vessels inside it that burned. רבי יהודה says he pays for everything that was inside. The חכמים say he pays only for a stack of wheat or a stack of barley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that states the same argument as our משנה. It is setting up the extra detail that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far this matches the משנה from step 10. The new information is the line that follows, which explains how the חכמים measure the payment.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who sets fire to a stack,
and there were vessels in it and they burned,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
he pays for everything that was inside it,
and the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם אֶלָּא גָּדִישׁ שֶׁל חִטִּין
phrases.english: he pays only for a stack of wheat
or a stack of barley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's explanation, the גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same מחלוקת that adds a calculation detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה says he pays for all contents. The חכמים say he pays only for the grain stack.

steps.title: How the payment is measured: treat the vessels' space as full of grain
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the space the vessels took up is treated as if it were full of grain. That way the owner is paid for a full stack.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we look at the place of the vessels as if it were full of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the חכמים calculate the payment when hidden vessels burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vessels took up space, so there was really less grain in the stack. Even so, the חכמים do not shrink the payment. They count the vessels' space as if grain filled it, so he pays for a full stack.

keyTerms.meaning: We view or regard, as the court calculates.
The space the vessels took up.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the חכמים make him pay for the vessels. He pays the price of grain for that space, not the value of the vessels.

phrases.english: And we view the place of the vessels
as if it were full of grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרוֹאִין מְקוֹם כֵּלִים כְּאִילּוּ הוּא מָלֵא תְּבוּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא by explaining how the חכמים's payment for a grain stack is calculated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vessels' space is valued as if it were filled with grain, and he pays for a full stack.
